news.title: American Otis to Install 125 Units at Morocco’s 115,000-Seat Grand Stade Hassan II
news.lede: Marrakech - Otis has been selected to supply and install 125 vertical-mobility units at the Grand Stade Hassan II, the Casablanca-area football venue Morocco is building for the 2030 FIFA World Cup. The New York-listed manufacturer announced the contract on November 11, describing itself as the world’s leading elevator and escalator company for manufacturing, installation, service, and modernization. The order spans four categories of equipment. Otis will install 73 Gen2 elevator systems, which it credits to flat-belt technology and a compact design for a smooth, quiet ride.

Ghanaian footballer Caleb Yirenkyi has earned a place in football history after the FIFA Museum added his torn Black Stars jersey to its collection of historic sporting memorabilia. The 20-year-old midfielder scored a dramatic late winner against Panama in Ghana's opening match at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

news.title: Romelu Lukaku retires from international football after 16-year Belgium career
news.lede: Belgium ’s all-time record goalscorer Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football at the age of 33. The forward made the announcement on Monday, a day after being an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1 in the Nations League.Lukaku had been named in the Red Devils' squad for this month's Nations League fixtures, but missed last Thursday’s 2-1 win over Turkey with a hop injury and then failed to make it off the bench against Italy.He scored 94 goals in 135 appearances for Belgium over a run that began with his debut in 2010. The former Chelsea and Manchester United striker revealed his decision in a statement on his official Instagram page.“. Over these 16 years, I gave everything for the national team,” Lukaku said.

news.title: European football body’s plan to go global leaves Fifa on tenterhooks
news.lede: Findings of ‘feasibility study’ into quest for world domination loom with Europe’s wealthiest certain to benefit whatever the outcome. It will be one of the most eagerly devoured documents in football circles, assuming its contents are ever fully revealed. In September, the increasingly powerful European Football Clubs body announced a “feasibility study” into how it can become established on a more global scale, morphing into an organisation that represents clubs all over the world. The study’s findings could, some leading figures in the sport’s governance believe, define football’s long-term future.

news.title: Vinicius reveals why his Real Madrid form has suffered this season
news.lede: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior has acknowledged that insufficient preparation and uncertainty over his future contributed to his disappointing start to the 2026/27 season. As reported by İdman.Biz, citing Reuters, the 26-year-old made the admission during a press conference ahead of Brazil's international friendly against Singapore. Vinicius explained that Brazil's early elimination from the 2026 World Cup had affected him emotionally, prompting him to spend more time resting and with his family during the summer break. "I ended up training less than in previous years," the Brazilian admitted, acknowledging that his reduced preparation may have influenced his early-season performances.

news.title: Morocco’s Amputee Football Team Reach World Cup Round of 16
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco's amputee football team has qualified for the Round of 16 of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup after defeating the United States 2-1 in their second Group E fixture on Sunday in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. The victory marked Morocco's second consecutive win in the competition, following an impressive 4-1 triumph over Uruguay in their opening match. Morocco made a strong start against the United States, scoring in the opening minute before doubling their advantage in the 27th minute. The Americans managed to reduce the deficit in the 46th minute, but the Moroccan side held on to secure all three points and confirm its qualification for the knockout stage.

news.title: Dino Sani dead at 94: Brazil legend and oldest surviving World Cup winner dies as emotional tribute paid
news.lede: BRAZILIAN football has been plunged into mourning after World Cup winner Dino Sani passed away aged 94. Sani, who helped his country lift their first-ever trophy at the 1958 finals, had been the oldest surviving World Cup winner. The midfielder played twice at the tournament in Sweden, including a 0-0 draw with England in Gothenburg. He starred for Argentine giants Boca Juniors before going to win a Serie A title and European Cup with AC Milan.
